definitions: The legal authority granted by a court to a conservator to manage the financial affairs, daily life, or both, of an individual deemed incapable of doing so themselves.
The legal right to make decisions on behalf of an incapacitated person regarding their estate, person, or both.
examples: The court granted the sister the power of conservatorship over her brother's estate.
Exercising the power of conservatorship, the guardian ensured the ward's medical bills were paid.
The family sought the power of conservatorship to protect their elderly parent from financial exploitation.
